title: Leadership team meeting agenda template (free, Word)
description: A free, editable agenda template for leadership team meetings: item types, desired outcomes, owners, time boxes, pre-reads and a short close.
lead: An agenda that says, for every item, what kind of item it is and what the owner wants from the team. It has a check to run before an item goes on, and a close that records decisions and actions. It is a Word file you can change as you like.
teaser: An agenda with a type and a desired outcome for every item, and a check before an item goes on. Its close records decisions, actions and how the meeting went.

items: **The meeting's frame:** date, chair, note-taker, the purpose of this meeting and the deadline for papers.
**The agenda table:** each item's type, the outcome the owner wants, the team task it serves, the owner, the time box and the pre-read.
**Four example items,** marked as examples, one of each type.
**A check before an item goes on:** four questions that keep issues off the agenda when they do not need the whole team.
**The close:** decisions and actions with owners and dates, parked items, and three short questions on how the meeting went.

blocks.text: What are the four item types?

head: Type
What the owner wants
A good desired outcome
rows: The team knows something, with time for questions
Everyone knows the main findings and has asked their questions.
Views and options, with no decision today
We understand the consequences for each unit before we decide next month.
A choice the team makes in the meeting
We agree the three priorities for the next quarter.
A check that earlier decisions are carried out
Each open action is on track, or has a new date.

blocks.text: Ask item owners to fill in their rows before a set deadline, with the pre-read attached. The chair then runs the check, and moves items that fail it to a better place.
In the meeting, read each item's type and desired outcome aloud before the discussion starts. It takes seconds, and it tells everyone what the item is for.

blocks.title: A rule of thumb
blocks.text: If an owner cannot write the desired outcome in one sentence, the item is not ready for the meeting.
Why is it built this way?

Research on top management meetings links clear goals for each item and focused discussion with better results. The reasons, with sources, are in [the leadership team meeting agenda](/articles/leadership-team-meeting-agenda) and [task conflict and relationship conflict](/articles/task-conflict-and-relationship-conflict).
